blog_summary: Adrian Colyer discusses the 'Raft Refloated' paper by Howard et al., which presents an independent implementation and rigorous evaluation of the Raft consensus protocol. The authors aim to assess Raft's claim of reducing cognitive complexity compared to alternatives like Paxos. They develop a production-quality Raft implementation in OCaml, complete with a distributed systems simulator and a formal model in Statecall Policy Language (SPL) to validate over 10,000 system traces. The paper highlights the challenges of building robust consensus systems, emphasizing the need for formal modeling, model checking, and careful instrumentation to avoid subtle bugs. The authors reproduce Raft's performance results and explore optimizations, demonstrating the value of simulation in uncovering rare but critical issues. While Raft's high-level concepts are found to be easier to understand than Paxos, the paper also reveals complexities in edge cases, such as livelocks, underscoring the difficulty of consensus protocol engineering.
paper_title: Raft Refloated: Do we have consensus?
